item.description: The main goal of this paper is to study the extension of genus-one BCOV type mirror symmetry for smooth projective varieties with vanishing $c_1(X)$. item.description: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. item.description: The \emph{minimum codegree} $\delta_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. item.description: We give an elementary proof of the determinant identity in \cite[Conjecture~A.1]{SYZ} over any field of odd characteristic $p$. The proof computes the determinant of a single linear map by dividing by two different monic polynomials. By \cite[Proposition~A.9]{SYZ}, the identity gives another proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo conjecture. The conjecture identifies the Higgs--de Rham self-map of the four-pointed projective line with the map induced by multiplication by $p$ on its elliptic double cover. — Jinbang Yang — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers
item.description: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here. — Stephan Rosebrock — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.description: We now live in the age of machine-generated mathematics: AI systems produce research-level proofs faster than the human mathematical community can read them. All of these require measuring distances between proofs. item.description: The generalized Tur\'an number $\ex(n,T,H)$ is the maximum number of $T$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no $H$. As applications, we determine the asymptotic value of $\ex(n,\{\text{ind-}C_4,C_{5}\})$ which answers a question of Ergemlidze, Gy\H{o}ri and Methuku, and the asymptotic value of 3-uniform hypergraph without Berge short cycle which solve a conjecture of Gy\H{o}ri and Salia. — Qing Cui, Ervin Gy\H{o}ri, Chenke Zhang, Xiutao Zhu — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM
